# Tysel

> Tysel is a lightweight native TypeScript runtime for services and AI agents. It packages an application and its runtime into one executable with explicit host capabilities and durable execution.

Tysel is Web-API-first and does not promise general Node.js compatibility.
There is no tagged binary release yet; the current installation path is a
source build. Do not infer stable public API status from internal milestone or
architecture records.

## Start

- [Documentation overview](https://tysel.dev/docs/): Choose a learning path and see the product contract at a glance.
- [Install Tysel](https://tysel.dev/docs/install/): Build from source now; understand the managed installer, diagnosis, upgrades, and rollback contract.
- [Getting started](https://tysel.dev/docs/getting-started/): Create, test, run, and package a Fetch-style HTTP service.
- [Guides](https://tysel.dev/docs/guides/): Find task-oriented paths for development, services, agents, shipping, and operations.
- [Example gallery](https://tysel.dev/docs/guides/examples/): Choose a complete runnable example by workload and execution profile.

## Learn

- [How Tysel works](https://tysel.dev/docs/concepts/how-tysel-works/): Follow source, validation, packaging, runtime ownership, and delivery.
- [Projects and configuration](https://tysel.dev/docs/concepts/projects-and-configuration/): Understand discovery, adoption, TOML/JSON manifests, conversion, and project tasks.
- [Execution profiles](https://tysel.dev/docs/concepts/execution-profiles/): Choose service, isolated, or experimental Component execution.
- [Durable execution](https://tysel.dev/docs/concepts/durable-execution/): Use replay-safe steps, effects, sleep, retry, signals, and persisted storage.

## Build

- [Runtime API](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/runtime/): Application exports, public TypeScript symbols, host capabilities, durable context, and tests.
- [Wasm Components](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/component/): Experimental language-neutral JSON tasks, Component ABI, restricted WASI, capabilities, and Rust/Go SDKs.
- [JavaScript APIs](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/javascript/): Supported server-side globals such as `fetch`, `Request`, and `WebSocket`.
- [Capability matrix](https://tysel.dev/docs/capabilities/): Availability of network, secrets, storage, files, WebSocket, LLM, and durable features by profile.
- [npm and Node.js compatibility](https://tysel.dev/docs/compatibility/): Dependency classification, unsupported runtime assumptions, and adoption checks.

## Reference

- [API reference index](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/): Find the authoritative surface for commands, configuration, APIs, and operational behavior.
- [CLI reference](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/cli/): Commands, options, defaults, side effects, structured output, and exit behavior.
- [Manifest reference](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/manifest/): Complete TOML/JSON schema concepts, permissions, limits, durable settings, and tasks.
- [Wasm Component reference](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/component/): Component task ABI, execution limits, filesystem capability imports, and guest SDK contracts.
- [Environment variables](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/environment/): Installation, capabilities, durable storage, LLM, telemetry, and host integration.
- [Limits and defaults](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/limits-and-defaults/): Configuration defaults and current runtime bounds.
- [Errors and machine output](https://tysel.dev/docs/reference/errors-and-output/): CLI streams, exit status, report behavior, and HTTP error envelopes.
- [JavaScript runtime compatibility notes](https://tysel.dev/docs/architecture/javascript-runtime-compatibility/): Rationale, evidence, and the full compatibility matrix.

## Operate and evaluate

- [Security model](https://tysel.dev/docs/security/): Effective authority, trust boundaries, deployment responsibilities, and non-goals.
- [Production operations](https://tysel.dev/docs/operations/production/): Release admission, deployment, secrets, backup, restore, capacity, monitoring, and incident response.
- [Performance and evidence](https://tysel.dev/docs/performance/): Benchmark gates, methodology, raw evidence, and claim restrictions.
- [Architecture](https://tysel.dev/docs/architecture/): System boundaries and current implementation map.
- [Architecture decisions](https://tysel.dev/docs/adr/): Design rationale for the runtime core, engine, Web API contract, delivery, capabilities, isolation, and durability.

## Source contracts

- [Tysel repository](https://github.com/wangcch/tysel): Source, schemas, examples, tests, and release tooling.
- [Manifest JSON Schema](https://github.com/wangcch/tysel/blob/main/crates/tysel-manifest/schema/tysel-manifest-v1.schema.json): Machine-readable application configuration contract.
- [TypeScript types](https://github.com/wangcch/tysel/tree/main/packages/tysel-types): Application-facing runtime declarations.
- [Runtime compatibility inventory](https://github.com/wangcch/tysel/blob/main/runtime-js/web-api/compatibility.json): Machine-readable Web API support data.
